scope: Proposition 4.6 (Operator with persistent defects) of the manuscript “Counterexamples to the Hahn-Wilson conjecture at height two” (preprints/Counterexamples-to-the-Hahn-Wilson-conjecture-at-height-two-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 319 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a90ada966eb41540), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under (4.8), there is a ∈ E0 satisfying (4.11) whose triangular matrix on Φ has the following properties. 1. For every fixed J ∈ Z, only finitely many matched pairs (l, j) satisfy l ≤ J < j. 2. There are constants c > 0 and N0 such that for every integer N ≥ N0, at least cNβ columns in [−N, 0] and at least cNβ rows in (0, N] are forever unmatched. Here the matching is that of Lemma 4.5; the constants may depend on p.
